sources.summary: UK Home Office country policy and information note: sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, June 2025. LGB people generally do not face a real risk of persecution from the state solely for sexual orientation, but people in the North Caucasus, trans people, and publicly active LGBT+ advocates are likely to face treatment amounting to persecution. Same-sex marriage and gender transition are banned nationwide. The 'gay propaganda' law carries administrative fines or detention up to 15 days, escalating to criminal prosecution on repeat (up to 4 years); the 2023 'extremist' designation of the international LGBT+ movement allows support/activity to be classed extremist (2-6 years; organising 6-10 years). At least 139 people were impacted by anti-LGBT+ laws 2022-2024; official reporting is restricted and data limited.
